paper.title_en: Asymptotic Throat as a Minimal Geometric Alternative to the Singularity in Schwarzschild Black Hole
paper.abstract_en: A basic question in the study of regular black holes is whether the Schwarzschild singularity can be replaced by a geodesically complete interior while retaining a single horizon. An asymptotic throat offers a minimal geometric realization of this possibility. The areal radius approaches a finite, nonzero limit at a future internal infinity, without requiring a change in spatial topology or a bounce. We extend the geometric analysis beyond monotone contraction to interiors in which the areal radius oscillates about its limit. For both null-type and spacelike-type inner ends, we derive a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for causal geodesic completeness and criteria for bounded curvature in parallel-propagated frames. Explicit examples of both types have complete inner ends and satisfy all four standard energy conditions at sufficiently large exterior radii. Applying these criteria to the oscillatory solution of the Böhmer--Vandersloot model of effective loop quantum gravity, we find a causally complete spacelike-type inner end. Its scalar curvature invariants converge to those of the limiting Nariai-type solution. Along each radial null geodesic, however, a parallel-propagated curvature component is unbounded along a sequence of turning points as the affine parameter tends to infinity.
